**(d) Constraint parametrizations.** Let a regular holonomic-constraint datum
$(O,k,g_{c})$ of [[def-cm06-holonomic-constraint-model]] be given, where
$g_{c}:=G$ is the constraint map called $G$ in that definition; this separate
notation distinguishes it from the kinetic matrix $G(q)$ in clause (b). Let
$\mathcal C\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ be its time-independent configuration
locus, so $\Sigma=\{(t,x)\in O:x\in\mathcal C\}$ (the scleronomic case).
A **parametrization of the constrained configurations** is a
generalized-coordinate map $X:\Omega\to Q$ with $r=3N-k$,
$X(\Omega)=\mathcal C\cap Q$, and $(t,X(q))\in O$ for all
$(t,q)\in I_{0}\times\Omega$. Thus $X$ covers every constrained configuration,
but a configuration may have more than one coordinate representative; a
covering or other surjective immersion is allowed. Injectivity is an optional
additional condition for applications that require unique coordinates. Each
admissible coordinate curve induces a constrained curve family with permitted
velocity; the reduction theorem of this page also identifies the virtual
displacements with the image of $DX$.

**(iii) The pivot constraint.** The material point of reference coordinate
$\rho_{p}:=-d\,e_{3}$ is the **pivot material point**; it lies on the
symmetry axis at distance $d$ from the centre of mass. The motions of the
branch are those satisfying
$$c(t)+R(t)\rho_{p}=0\qquad(t\in I_{0}),$$
    that is $c(t)=d\,R(t)e_{3}$: the pivot material point is held fixed at the
    origin of the inertial frame for the whole time window, and the centre of
    mass lies on the sphere of radius $d$ about the origin. The
constraint is maintained by a mechanism (a bearing, a hinge or a fine
support) whose force system is **ideal** in the sense adopted for
frictionless hinges in [[post-cm06-ideal-reaction-law]] clause (iii) together
with the virtual-work law of its clause (i): the mechanism exerts on the body
a force system equivalent to a single force applied at the pivot point, so
that its total torque about the origin **vanishes**. The holonomic-constraint
vocabulary of [[def-cm06-holonomic-constraint-model]] — constrained curve
families, reaction fields and the declaration that the constraint is
maintained by an additional force contribution — is the framework's account
for finitely many particle labels; the present model is a continuum, and this
clause adopts the analogous idealisation for it. No friction, damping or
driving torque at the pivot is asserted; such torques are excluded and would
have to be declared as part of a torque datum with their own model.

This page adds the constrained and moving-chart branches to the force model
of [[cm02-forces-initial-data-and-newtonian-flow]]. The holonomic branch
begins with [[def-cm06-holonomic-constraint-model]]: a regular
holonomic-constraint datum $(O,k,G)$ with a nonempty constraint locus
$\Sigma$ on which $D_{x}G$ has rank $k$, the constrained curve families and
permitted velocities, the virtual displacements $\ker D_{x}G$, the reaction
field and the equation of the constrained branch
$\mathsf Mx''=F(t,x,w)+R$, the consistent data, and the
scleronomic/rheonomic classification of the locus. For a specified constrained curve the reaction is the unique residual
$R=\mathsf Mx^{\prime\prime}-F(t,x,x^{\prime})$. The additional idealization that
selects the dynamically admissible constrained curves is the adopted postulate
[[post-cm06-ideal-reaction-law]]: the reaction annihilates every virtual
displacement at fixed time, equivalently it is the transpose multiple
$D_{x}G^{\mathsf T}\lambda$ of the constraint Jacobian, with the same
restriction intended for frictionless joints, smooth tracks and taut links
and excluded for sliding friction, unilateral and contact-change mechanisms,
rank loss and direct active forces on the labels along permitted displacements.
Prescribed support motion is encoded in a time-dependent constraint and may
transfer energy through the ideal reaction; driving-equipment dynamics remain
outside the model.
